newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens 1st-half 96/97 flat at 1.08 bln DM.
newsitem.headline: Siemens 1st-half 96/97 flat at 1.08 bln DM.

text.p: German industrial group Siemens AG on Wednesday reported group after-tax profit in the first half of 1996/97 to 1.08 billion marks ($630.8 million), compared to 1.083 billion marks the year before.

First-half group sales rose to 44.7 billion marks, versus 42.3 billion marks in the 1995/96, which ended September 30. Orders in the period rose 53.9 billion marks from the year-ago figure of 48.6 billion marks, the company said in a statement. ($ = 1.712 German Marks)
Siemens also said it would maintained its forecast of no increase in group profit for 1996/97.
In November Siemens said profit would not rise because falling semiconductor prices would cause a decline in results in its chip-making unit, one of its most profitable businesses.
The company said it invested 3.9 billion marks in the first half, up from 3.4 billion marks invested in the first six months of 1995/96.
As of March 31, Siemens' payroll of 379,000 workers worldwide was unchanged from September.
